correctness.rationale: Taking the graded invariants gives the asserted equation. The projective fixed loci are v=0 (a smooth fixed quintic with reflection action in its normal direction) and the isolated point in the v-chart. At the latter the u derivative is 5 and the remaining smooth coordinates z,w are acted on by simultaneous sign, yielding exactly one A1 point. Weighted adjunction, crepancy and the invariant summand of H^1 of the quintic, preserved by resolution of the rational singularity, give K3. The degree-two sections have no common zero; pullback from the ample Cartier O_Y(2) gives nef and big, with only E contracted. The square is 10 and cannot be divisible by the square of any integer at least 2. Locally on the resolution use q=z/w and p=w^2: the exceptional is p=0 and the five strict transforms are q=beta with distinct simple roots. The equation at v=1 gives u as w^5(q^5+1) times a unit; u^2 pulls back to order 5 on p=0 and order 2 on each arm. Thus the divisor identity is integral and linear, not just numerical. Adjunction and the Schur complement give the star's signature and determinant. The t=0 plane quintic is disjoint from o, maps isomorphically from the fixed curve, and is a genus-six member of H. Coordinate permutations and diagonal fifth-root scalings give the stated conjugacies. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/finite_checks.py 1 checks the polynomial, square completion, local leading form and lattice identities; the geometric assertions are proved analytically.
residual_risks: The configuration is a sublattice, not an assertion about its saturation or the full Néron–Severi group.

value.rationale: The classified Fermat involutions motivate asking what surface one obtains. The integral nef genus-six polarization and all six named curves, rather than just the K3 label, provide useful geometric data for classifying or comparing the model and its degree-two alternative.
